Command: Do not offer honey on the altar
Summary: The command: Do not offer honey on the altar (Leviticus 2:11). No honey might be burned as an offering made by fire on the altar.
Commandment: Do not offer honey on the altar.
Application: This row narrows the parent group command to this one mitzvah. The moral/ceremonial/civil division is a traditional classification, not Scripture's own division; this law is traditionally classed as ceremonial. Hebrews teaches these sacrifices could never perfect the worshiper; they pointed forward to Christ's once-for-all offering, which is why they ceased with the new covenant.
Purpose: To provide atonement, thanksgiving, and fellowship under the old covenant. Hebrews teaches these pointed forward to Christ's once-for-all offering (Hebrews 10:1-14), so the system ceased.
Function: No honey might be burned as an offering made by fire on the altar — a ceremonial law of the excluded sweet. Its goal was to keep the altar's fire free of honey, the sweet kept off the fire as the leaven was. Scripture gives no particular evil this restrained beyond the guarding of the altar itself, and I will not invent one; its work was order and reverence, not restraint. The altar took only what God appointed, and honey was not among it.
